newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks off highs in overbought market.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks off highs in overbought market.

text.p: Wall Street stocks retreated from their highs in late morning trading as an overbought stock market failed to sustain a rally.

The Dow industrials were up 13 points at 7150 after having rallied as high as 7196. Advances led declines by two to one. U.S. Treasuries remained firm, with the long bond up 17/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The NYSE said it lifted its curbs on index-arbitrage trades at 1036 EDT/1436 GMT.
Analysts said that the rally had been sparked by comments made by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan yesterday.

"You can tell the market is overbought because it is not responding to good news, or what it interprets as good news," said Phil Roth, chief technical analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds. "People thought that Greenspan was intimating that he wouldn't be as hard towards interest rates as he was before. That remains to be seen. What we are seeing today is a normal consolidation."

Cephalon Inc was among the day's losers. Shares fell eight to 12 after the company's treatment for Lou Gehrig's disease was rejected by a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel. ((--A.G. Wall Street desk 212-859-1737))
